chunks: Say: "To whom does the earth and whosoever is upon it belong, if you know?"
ai.seo_question: Who is the true owner of the earth and its inhabitants according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Mu'minun, this rhetorical question challenges polytheists to identify any rival deity who shares in the creation and ownership of the earth, thereby isolating Allah as the sole Sovereign (Malik). Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai, emphasize that this verse establishes the logical prerequisite for divine legislation: since Allah is the absolute Owner, He alone possesses the right to be the Lawgiver (Shari'). This reinforces the concept of Tawhid in Dominion (Tawhid al-Malik) as the foundation for accepting prophetic authority.
